summary: SendGrid's Email API is a documented REST v3 Web API authenticated with permission-scoped API keys sent as Bearer tokens. New accounts can self-serve a 60-day trial with up to 100 Email API emails per day, then need a paid Email API plan to continue sending; upgrade requires two-factor authentication, domain authentication, and a payment method. Composio lists the exact SENDGRID toolkit. No SendGrid-operated execution MCP server was verified: SendGrid's MCP documentation route renders a 404, Twilio's hosted MCP is a read-only documentation server, and the community SendGrid MCP project is third-party.
blocker: Sending stops after the 60-day trial unless an Email API plan is purchased. API keys are permission-scoped and displayed only once. No vendor SendGrid execution MCP endpoint or transport was verified, so a build should use the REST API or an official SDK rather than Twilio's documentation MCP or a community server.
next_action: Create a SendGrid trial account, enable two-factor authentication, authenticate a sending domain, and create a Restricted Access API key limited to Mail Send plus only the additional scopes required. Prototype POST https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/mail/send with verified sender identities and budget a paid Email API plan before day 60. Recheck official MCP documentation before considering MCP, and do not substitute Twilio's documentation MCP or third-party servers.

value: SendGrid Email API v3: API key in an HTTP Authorization header as Bearer <API key>
Permission-scoped API keys: Full Access, Custom Access, or separate Billing Access; Mail Send can be restricted
auth.reason: The undated official authentication page requires an HTTP Authorization header containing an API Key and documents Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY_HERE>. The undated API Keys page documents Full Access, Custom Access, Billing Access, creator-permission limits, and one-time key display. The undated Email API quickstart documents a Restricted Access key with Mail Send > Full Access. The docs.sendgrid.com evidence routes rendered through 301 redirects to the corresponding Twilio SendGrid documentation; quotes are from the rendered final pages.

This combines a self-serve trial with a paid continuation gate. The cited documentation and support article are undated.

The separate Campaigns API page states that it covers the obsolete Legacy Marketing Campaigns API, so legacy campaign endpoints are not conflated with the Email API/Mail Send surface. official_mcp.reason: Scoped documentation review of SendGrid's official MCP route, merged SendGrid/Twilio product page, and Twilio's official MCP documentation found no vendor server for SendGrid execution. The SendGrid MCP route returns 404 and the product page contains no MCP server text. Twilio's hosted MCP is a read-only documentation server that indexes SendGrid docs but does not connect to an account or execute API calls, so it is not a SendGrid execution server. This is a point-in-time documentation finding, not a universal absence claim. The SendGrid pages are undated; Twilio labels its MCP Public Beta without a publication date.

verdict.reason: A scoped API-key authentication method, a self-serve 60-day trial, and a broad REST Email API are documented, so a direct REST or official-SDK build is viable. Continued sending requires a paid Email API plan after the trial, with two-factor authentication, domain authentication, and a payment method before upgrade. Legacy Marketing Campaigns is separate and obsolete. No SendGrid execution MCP is verified, so this verdict rests on REST rather than MCP. The load-bearing documentation and support pages are undated.
